acceptance_evidence: per-stage retry (mandatory): p4t4-per-stage-retry.test.ts — every stage method is idempotent: re-running any completed stage performs ZERO seam writes and ZERO external-adapter re-calls (exact write deltas asserted: allocate=1 op PREPARED row; createChildSession=2 child record + member record; bindChildSession=1 binding; commitInstance=4 ledger counter boot + counter bump + fact + COMMITTED row; full provision=8); self-ensuring entry (commitInstance/bindChildSession from a fresh world drive the FULL chain); idempotency guard: same member + different allocationToken / changed label -> RECORD_DUPLICATE + details.problem idempotency-conflict with 0 writes and still exactly one committed member; same-request replay = 0-write no-op with the same ledgerSequence=1

orphan detect (mandatory): p4t4-orphan-detect.test.ts — a durably recorded child with an uncommitted member is a DIAGNOSABLE orphan (ORPHANED_CHILD_SESSION, context.missing names the exact missing pieces): S2 CHILD_SESSION_CREATED -> ['binding','commit']; S3/S4 CHILD_BOUND -> ['commit']; B4 crash after child create -> ['record','binding','commit']; ALLOCATED without child is NOT an orphan (the external effect has not happened — nothing was recorded externally); listOrphans() is team-scoped via the operation intent payload-root filter (two coordinators over one shared domain each list only their own orphan) and sorted by instanceId (multi-member case asserts alpha-before-beta with per-orphan missing sets); the orphan clears exactly when recovery commits the member

one-committed-instance invariant (mandatory): p4t4-one-committed-invariant.test.ts Part 2 — never two committed for one (rootSessionId, instanceId): same-request replay 0 writes; different allocationToken / changed label -> loud idempotency conflict, no writes, one committed alpha + one fact; a SECOND member (inst-beta) in the same team commits independently (2 members, 2 facts, exactly one committed per instance); the SAME instanceId under a DIFFERENT root over the SAME shared domain derives a DIFFERENT deterministic operationId and commits independently (3 facts total) — per-(root,instance) committed count is always exactly one

10-boundary fault-injection matrix (DevPlan §17.4 frozen table, plan lines 2267-2290): p4t4-one-committed-invariant.test.ts Part 1 — fresh world per boundary; crash = seam armed (setCrashAfterWrites) mid-`provision` + RE-DRIVE via `recover` (real process crashes are P4-T5's job). Seam-write map (fresh world): W1 op PREPARED, W2 child recorded, W3 member record, W4 binding, W5 counter boot, W6 counter bump, W7 fact, W8 COMMITTED row. B1 before op prepare=offset 0 (recovery 8 writes; the external effect never fired: createCalls 0 -> 1); B2 after op prepare=offset 1 AND B3 before child create=offset 1 — SAME seam boundary, documented honestly: the adapter call performs NO seam write, so the child is already minted on the adapter side but unrecorded in TeamDomain (status ALLOCATED, no orphan); re-drive re-mints the SAME deterministic child (createCalls 2, childrenCreated stays 1); B4 after child create=2 (recovery 6; the recorded child is REUSED — adapter not re-called); B5 before SessionBinding=3 (5); B6 before MemberInstance commit=4 AND B8 before ledger=4 — same seam state (the ledger write is the first commit write), recovery 4; B7 after MemberInstance commit=8 NO crash (the 8-write protocol completes); B9 before operation committed=7 (recovery 1: the fact is already durable, only the COMMITTED row is missing — 'committed' requires BOTH halves, so pre-recovery status is CHILD_BOUND + orphan, not committed); B10 after committed=8 NO crash. Every row converges to: exactly 1 member, 1 fact, operation row COMMITTED with the stable deterministic operationId, 0 orphans, childrenCreated 1, and a post-recovery no-op of 0 writes

notes: No P4-T1/T2/T3 defects found: the P4-T2 journal (prepare/recordChildSession/applyPhase/drive, child-session-conflict, idempotency-conflict), the P4-T3 SessionBindingService preconditions, the P4-T1 in-memory seam fake, and the contracts all behave exactly as documented; the one 'invalid root id' failure during debugging was MY test expectation being wrong, not a production defect (root session ids are opaque upstream — structural rule only: non-empty, <=255, no control chars, no whitespace per contracts ids/session-id.ts — so 'not-a-root' is a VALID opaque id and provisioningOperationId rightly accepts it; the test now uses '' and 'root with space' for root violations). Locked design decisions: (1) 'committed' = operation row COMMITTED AND the ledger fact exists (both halves; the B9 crash leaves the fact durable but the row PREPARED -> NOT committed, an orphan naming ['commit']); (2) the member record is written at the CHILD_SESSION_CREATED stage (lifecycle CREATED) because the P4-T3 binding service requires the record to exist before binding; (3) the operationId is a deterministic FNV-1a base36 token of BOTH root and instance, so the same instanceId under two teams never collides in the global operations store (cross-team same-domain case asserted); (4) ALLOCATED-without-child is NOT an orphan (no external effect yet); the narrow adapter has no list-children method by design (R20), so an externally-minted-but-unrecorded child (the B2/B3 window) is diagnosable only via re-drive convergence in P4 — runtime cross-check is P5's job.
